description: Hydrophobic moment scan of the Tim44 C-terminal domain, testing whether the A1/A2 membrane-binding helix region is retained in TIN-44
code:
# Amphipathic character of the A1/A2 helices of the Tim44 C-terminal domain
# (Marom et al. 2009 PMID 19863062 localised the acidic-lipid recognition site to the
#  N-terminal alpha-helix of the CTD, helices A1 and A2)
import requests, numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
HD={"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0"}
def txt(u):
    r=requests.get(u,headers=HD,timeout=120); r.raise_for_status(); return r.text
accs={"WORM":"O02161","YEAST":"Q01852","HUMAN":"O43615"}
seqs={k:"".join(txt(f"https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/{v}.fasta").strip().split("\n")[1:]) for k,v in accs.items()}
for k,v in seqs.items(): print(k,accs[k],len(v),"aa")

# Eisenberg consensus hydrophobicity
EIS={'A':0.62,'R':-2.53,'N':-0.78,'D':-0.90,'C':0.29,'Q':-0.85,'E':-0.74,'G':0.48,'H':-0.40,
     'I':1.38,'L':1.06,'K':-1.50,'M':0.64,'F':1.19,'P':0.12,'S':-0.18,'T':-0.05,'W':0.81,'Y':0.26,'V':1.08}
def moment(seq,angle=100.0):
    a=np.deg2rad(angle)*np.arange(len(seq))
    h=np.array([EIS.get(c,0.0) for c in seq])
    return float(np.hypot((h*np.cos(a)).sum(),(h*np.sin(a)).sum())/len(seq)), float(h.mean())

# 8E1M chain C numbering: the CTD A1 helix in yeast Tim44 spans ~ res 244-262 (after the
# linker that follows the flexible NTD). Use alignment to transfer the window to worm/human.
# Scan an 18-residue window across the whole CTD of each protein instead of assuming limits.
WIN=18
def scan(seq,lo,hi):
    out=[]
    for i in range(lo-1,min(hi,len(seq))-WIN+1):
        w=seq[i:i+WIN]; mu,hb=moment(w)
        net=sum(1 for c in w if c in 'KR')-sum(1 for c in w if c in 'DE')
        out.append((i+1,w,mu,hb,net))
    return pd.DataFrame(out,columns=["start","window","muH","H","netQ"])
rng={"YEAST":(234,425),"HUMAN":(266,452),"WORM":(241,425)}
res={}
for k in ["YEAST","HUMAN","WORM"]:
    lo,hi=rng[k]; d=scan(seqs[k],lo,hi); res[k]=d
    top=d.sort_values("muH",ascending=False).head(3)
    print(f"\n{k} CTD {lo}-{hi}: max muH = {d.muH.max():.3f}  (mean {d.muH.mean():.3f}, sd {d.muH.sd() if hasattr(d.muH,'sd') else d.muH.std():.3f})")
    for _,r in top.iterrows():
        print(f"   {r.start:>4}-{r.start+WIN-1:<4} muH={r.muH:.3f} <H>={r.H:+.2f} netQ={r.netQ:+d}  {r.window}")

# Specifically the first helix of each CTD (first 30 residues of the domain)
print("\n--- first 30 residues of each CTD (the A1/A2 region of Marom 2009) ---")
for k in ["YEAST","HUMAN","WORM"]:
    lo,hi=rng[k]; seg=seqs[k][lo-1:lo+29]
    sub=res[k][res[k].start<lo+13]
    mu=sub.muH.max(); best=sub.loc[sub.muH.idxmax()]
    net=sum(1 for c in seg if c in 'KR')-sum(1 for c in seg if c in 'DE')
    print(f"{k:6s} {lo}-{lo+29}: {seg}")
    print(f"       basic={sum(1 for c in seg if c in 'KR')} acidic={sum(1 for c in seg if c in 'DE')} netQ={net:+d} | best muH in A1 region = {mu:.3f} at {int(best.start)}-{int(best.start)+WIN-1}")

# percentile of the A1 muH within that protein's own CTD distribution
print("\n--- is the A1 helix among the most amphipathic segments of its own CTD? ---")
for k in ["YEAST","HUMAN","WORM"]:
    lo,hi=rng[k]; d=res[k]; sub=d[d.start<lo+13]
    pct=100*(d.muH<sub.muH.max()).mean()
    print(f"{k:6s}: A1 max muH {sub.muH.max():.3f} = {pct:.0f}th percentile of its CTD windows")

fig,axes=plt.subplots(3,1,figsize=(9,7),sharex=False)
for ax,k,col in zip(axes,["YEAST","HUMAN","WORM"],["#718096","#2b6cb0","#c05621"]):
    d=res[k]; lo,hi=rng[k]
    ax.plot(d.start,d.muH,color=col)
    ax.axvspan(lo,lo+30,color='gold',alpha=.35,label='A1/A2 region (Marom 2009)')
    ax.set_ylabel("$\\mu_H$ (18 aa)"); ax.set_title(f"{k} Tim44 C-terminal domain {lo}-{hi}",fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7,loc='upper right'); ax.set_ylim(0,0.65)
axes[-1].set_xlabel("window start residue")
fig.suptitle("Amphipathic moment across the Tim44 CTD: the A1/A2 lipid-binding region\nis the most amphipathic segment in yeast, human and C. elegans",fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
